title: Tone, rate and mirroring
header_line: My analysis of one book on negotiation. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What does your voice do when someone upsets you?
I asked: what do we learn? We learn about tone, rate, pacing and leading. What is mirroring?
A student said that it gets you a better understanding of their point, or helps them feel more understood and heard.
I said: it is empathy, creating an emotional bridge, a mutual understanding.

groups.heading: Do not take the unnecessary risk

lines.text: I discussed a story in the book where the negotiator asked a suspect directly if he was a named person. A student said that being direct can give you tells; I said it was a massive and unnecessary risk, and that afterwards the negotiator used a calm, downward voice to put him at ease.

I role-played a hard conversation with a student: I accused the student of a management and execution problem. The student answered calmly, saying he was in it for the long term and asking what the solution would be.
I said that the tone was good, the rate could have been slower, and that I did not see any buying of time, such as saying: that is interesting, let me process what you just said.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the tone you use when you are upset.
Write the rate you want instead.
Write what mirroring would sound like in your next hard talk.
Write the risk you will not take.

check.q: What did a student say mirroring does?
What did I say the direct question was?
What did I say to do to buy time?
choices: Say: let me process what you just said

recap: Slow your rate. Mirror. Buy time. Skip unnecessary risk.
